//: Rules for the nodes added by the update and notification features.
WHY THIS MATTERS: the project's current rules are
{ ".read": "auth.uid != null", ".write": "auth.uid != null" }
so ANY signed-in user can write anywhere. With the new features that now
means any of your 1,400+ users could queue a push notification to
everyone, or point every installed app at a web bundle of their choosing.
That is worth closing.
HOW TO APPLY: open the Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules,
and merge the three blocks below into the rules you already have, keeping
your existing top-level ".read" and ".write". Child rules override the
parent, so the rest of the database keeps behaving exactly as it does now
and the old Android app is unaffected — it never touches these nodes.
Merge the indexes from database.rules.indexes.json at the same time if you
have not already.

update.//: Everyone reads which version to run; only admins decide it.

//: Only admins may queue a push. Nobody needs to read the queue except
the GitHub Actions sender, which uses the service account and bypasses
rules entirely.
A device token is a way to send that person notifications, so each
user writes only their own, and nobody can read the whole list. The
admin panel's device count is the one thing this costs: it will show
zero unless you are signed in as an admin, hence the read rule.
